description: SUPERSEDED - DO NOT RUN. This workflow cannot finish on a 62 GB machine: it was OOM-killed on shot fourteen after 92 minutes. Every completed step is retained as a previous_result, about 460 MB a shot, on top of a ~51 GB resident H3 pipeline. Use MarmotCroonsFullA.json and MarmotCroonsFullB.json (eight shots each) followed by MarmotCroonsStitch.json, which produce a byte-identical edit. Kept only for the shot design and prompts below. MarmotCroons across the whole 81.5 s recording: sixteen 124-frame shots cut together, built on the four-shot MarmotCroonsCut which verified sample-exact sync and no degradation over its length. Every shot is generated fresh from the same supplied portrait and its own frame-exact slice of the song, so nothing is carried forward and nothing accumulates - the sixteenth shot is as clean as the first. The song is resampled once to the audio VAE's 32 kHz for conditioning while the soundtrack laid over the finished edit stays the untouched 44.1 kHz recording, so sync is sample-accurate by construction rather than maintained across sixteen seams. Conditioning runs off a centre-extracted vocal isolate: with the full mix the mouth mimes through instrumental passages, and the isolate is the only change that stopped it. The shot order is cut to the song rather than to a rhythm. A mid/side vocal-presence map of the recording found the voice present in only 41% of 250 ms cells overall and very unevenly spread, and H3 follows supplied audio loosely, so close-ups are placed only on windows measured strongly sung - 0-21 s and 62-67 s - while the sparsest windows get shots the mouth is not in at all: the paws on the stand at 36-41 s, a wide from the back of the empty room at 52-57 s, and an over-the-shoulder from behind at 67-72 s. The last shot runs 1.1 s past the end of the recording; slice_audio zero-pads it, so the song finishes and the frame holds in silence. Every shot prompt states that <Picture 1> carries no compositional detail - without that, H3's omni-reference reproduces the reference image's own composition and every cut lands on the same framing.
